intended_object: The canonical S-algebra isomorphism S ⊗_R R[1/r] ≅ S[1/r], where r ∈ R and R → S is an algebra map: localization commutes with base change. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition works over arbitrary commutative semirings R and S. A can be any R-algebra that satisfies `IsLocalization.Away r A`, so it is not limited to the specific model `Localization.Away r`. The instance `IsLocalization.Away.tensor`, stated just before it, shows that S ⊗[R] A is a localization of S away from the image of r. The definition then applies `IsLocalization.algEquiv`, the canonical isomorphism between two localizations of S at `Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R S r)`, to get an isomorphism onto `Localization.Away (algebraMap R S r)`.

This is the standard isomorphism S ⊗_R R_r ≅ S_r. It is S-linear and canonical, because it is determined by the universal property of localization. The generality is the natural one: commutative semirings and any model of the localization. I found no other Mathlib declaration that defines exactly this isomorphism. Related constructions such as `IsLocalization.Away.tensorProductEquivTMulRight` handle a different variant.
